title: Motor Line Decoder
description: Learners interpret each of the ten fields of the motor line '50 HP, 1800 RPM, IN, P, 3 Phase, 60 Frequency, 460 Volt, SD, TEFC, 326T', picking one of four meanings before the explanation is revealed. The decoded meaning stays under each field, misconception picks get a one-line note, and the whole line ends decoded with the first-try score.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Reading a fan motor specification line
learningObjectives: The learner will interpret each of the ten fields of a Twin City Fan motor specification line, choosing the correct meaning for at least 8 of 10 fields on the first attempt.
prerequisites: NEMA frame size and frame letters

accessibility.notes: Native buttons for every meaning and answered field; verdicts, field changes and reopened explanations announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs, solid/dashed borders and the ▸ current-field marker pair with colour; keys 1-4 pick, Enter goes to the next field; focus moves to Next field after a pick and to the first meaning on a new field.

controls.label: Four meanings (1-4)
controls.purpose: Pick the meaning of the highlighted field; one scored pick per field

controls.label: Next field / Show decoded line
controls.purpose: Advances to the next field (Enter); after field 10 shows the decoded line and score

controls.label: Answered field in the line
controls.purpose: Reopens that field's explanation (exploration, not scored)

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Clears the score and returns to field 1

equations: Shaft height = first two frame digits / 4 (in.)
rules: Ten fields in fixed order; each shows four choices in a fixed shuffled order.
A first pick is correct when it equals the field's meaning; the score counts first picks only.
Mastery is 8 or more of 10 correct on the first attempt.
assumptions: Distractor meanings are illustrative and are not real codes.
limitations: Decodes one example line; it does not cover EC lines, IEC frames or other duty codes in depth.

sources: Source: FanPedia p. 71 (typical motor specification line and field categories)
Source: FanPedia pp. 72-74 (efficiency, enclosure and duty, frame letters)
Shaft-height rule: standard NEMA relationship for foot-mounted frames from 143T up

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict each field's meaning, then reveal the explanation; the decoded line accumulates field by field
keyQuestions: Why is 1800 RPM not the motor's running speed?
Which field is efficiency, and which is phase?
What does the T in 326T tell you, and what is the shaft height?
commonMisconceptions: 1800 RPM is the exact running speed.
assessmentOpportunities: First-try score shown as 'First-try correct: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
